objective_scope.walk: simple random walk on a finite simple undirected unweighted graph
objective_scope.target: at least one within-part missing edge has K(G+e)-K(G)<=0

proposed_theorem: Every edge added within a minimum-size non-singleton part has K(G+e)-K(G)<0.
proof_method: Apply Hu-Kirkland Theorem 3.2.3 to a relabeled minimum part, clear only positive denominators, and certify the resulting numerator as the negative of a 124-term strictly positive-coefficient polynomial in x-3, y-x, z-x, and p-1.

finite_diagnostic.scope: sanity check only; not proof of the universal quantifier

limitations: The authoring branch cannot certify the final mathematical gate.
No claim is made for p=0 or more than three non-singleton parts.
Current publication novelty is unresolved and requires later primary-literature review.
No real-world impact, performance, or broad graph-family claim follows from this proof candidate alone.
